AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Direct immunofluorescence microscopy (DIF) of a skin biopsy specimen is the reference standard for the diagnosis of pemphigoid diseases (PD). Serration pattern analysis enables differentiation of epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) from other PD using DIF microscopy alone. However, practice gaps need to be addressed for implication of this technique in daily routine diagnostics.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: to determine and optimize the technical requirements for serration pattern analysis of DIF microscopy and determine inter-rater conformity of serration pattern analysis.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: we compared serration pattern analysis of routine DIF from Groningen and Lübeck laboratories with four blinded observers. Skin biopsies from 20 patients with EBA and other PD were exchanged and analysed. Various factors of section thickness, transport medium and biopsy processing were evaluated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: inter-rater conformity of four observers was 95.7%. Recognition of serration patterns was comparable in samples transported in saline and in Michel's medium and with section thicknesses of 4, 6 and 8 μm.

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATIONS
AbstractText.content: sample size and availability of 20 samples retrospectively compared.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: DIF serration pattern analysis is not restricted by variation in laboratory procedures, transport medium, or experience of observers. This learnable technique can be implemented as routine diagnostic method in extension to DIF microscopy for subtyping PD.
